highlights.title: Florida cops say they don't know who owns 11 unpermitted Flock cameras
highlights.summary: Florida cops are facing questions after a mandate to remove all Flock cameras tracking cars on St. Lucie County roads led local police to uncover more than a dozen suspicious cameras operating without permits.
body: Local residents told The Washington Post that they were alarmed that no one knows who owns many of the mysterious cameras.

Of the 14 cameras found, 11 had no obvious owners, raising concerns about who has access to sensitive data that bad actors could abuse. After the cameras were discovered, St. Lucie County Commissioner James Clasby told a local news outlet that there’s “potential for non-law enforcement to have cameras out there, and I’m not OK with that.”

But the St. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office ended up claiming three of those cameras, then refused to explain why they never obtained the required permits. The office did not immediately respond to Ars’ request to clarify whether it ever accessed data recorded by the cameras.

In Florida, police have repeatedly been caught misusing Flock cameras, sometimes tracking single cars hundreds of times for personal reasons. One officer in Fort Pierce, Josepher Crutchfield, accessed a Flock database 382 times while stalking an ex-girlfriend, the Post noted, while another cop, Christopher Goodson, reportedly nearly doubled that number of searches while looking for his estranged wife.

highlights.title: Judge dismisses antitrust lawsuits over Google’s AI Overviews
highlights.summary: A federal judge has dismissed a pair of antitrust lawsuits filed by Chegg and Rolling Stone parent company Penske Media Corporation, which accused Google of driving away web traffic with its AI-powered search features, as reported earlier by Reuters.
body: Rolling Stone’s parent company and Chegg claimed Google’s AI search features drove away traffic from their sites.

In lawsuits filed last year, Chegg and PMC accused Google of abusing its monopoly power by coercing publishers into supplying content for AI Overviews for free, or risk disappearing from search results. The publishers alleged Google’s practices diverted traffic away from their sites, hurting their revenue.

Judge Mehta, who made a landmark antitrust ruling against Google in 2024, disagrees with Chegg and PMC’s claims. “Plaintiffs have pleaded only that they have an ‘expectation’ that Google will send them search ​traffic if they make their content available for free,” Mehta writes. “But an expectation is not an agreement. It is simply how a general search engine works.”

Mehta adds that the court is not “unsympathetic to the situation publishers now find themselves in,” but writes that antitrust rules can’t replace a legislative body’s decision to address the economic impact of “new innovation.”

highlights.title: How Man City plan to argue their innocence in appeal
highlights.summary: Manchester City will argue in their Premier League appeal that the extra funding for their sponsorship deals between 2009 and 2018 came from the Abu Dhabi government and not the club's owners.
body: An independent commission has found that City broke Premier League financial rules by disguising £830.69m of owner funding as sponsorship income.
City's lawyers argued during the 2024 hearing that the funding had come from the Abu Dhabi government, but this was rejected by the commission.
In their judgement the commission "concluded that it was an explanation that the club had concocted well after the event in an attempt to conceal the realities of the Disguised Funding Scheme".
Manchester City is majority owned by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan's Newton Investment and Development LLC.

highlights.title: Ruriko-ji Temple location in Forza Horizon 6
highlights.summary: Ruriko-ji Temple is one of the many landmarks and photography locations in Forza Horizon 6, and it's also featured in a few Festival Playlist challenges, like the #TempleVantage photo challenge in the "British Automotive" series.
body: As the Forza Horizon 6 map is huge, it can be quite difficult to find any landmark, let alone a temple in the woods. However, don't let that sway you from visiting Ruriko-ji Temple, as it's one of the best photo locations to show off your car.
Ruriko-ji Temple is located in the northwest corner of the Minamino region, just south of the farms at the top of the area.

Ruriko-ji Temple is an easy landmark to miss, as there aren't many races or challenges nearby. The easiest way to get there is to follow the off-road trail on the west side of the Naruo Golf Course all the way up until you eventually hit the temple. However, if you've already been to the temple, you can fast travel to any road near it instead to save some time.

While you're here, make sure to take a photo of the temple to earn credit for it in the Photography section of the Discovery journal. However, make sure you're taking a photo of the temple, rather than the pagoda beside it, or else you won't receive credit.

highlights.title: Video Games Europe hits back at EU watchdog targeting King, Supercell, Mojang and more over IAP practices
highlights.summary: The EU’s Consumer Protection Cooperation Network has launched coordinated enforcement actions against games companies including King, Supercell, Mojang, Riot Games, Activision Blizzard and Ubisoft, over how they sell and handle in-game virtual currencies.
body: The CPC Network brings together national consumer protection authorities from across the EU and EEA and is coordinated by the European Commission. In a joint statement published September 30, it said it had found that “a high number of video game companies” had made no substantive changes to their practices since it published non-binding “Key Principles” on in-game currencies in March 2025, despite extensive subsequent talks with industry bodies.

It said the coordinated actions are particularly focused on compliance around variable reward systems such as loot boxes, “dark patterns” and other “harmful influencing techniques”, and practices that directly exhort children to spend money, which it says EU law already prohibits.
Video Games Europe and the European Game Developers Federation pushed back on the CPC Network’s actions in a statement also published on September 30.

highlights.title: Google rolls out new Gemini AI model but restricts access over safety concerns
highlights.summary: Tech company releases Gemini 4 Argon only to a vetted group of cybersecurity experts to avoid misuse by hackers. Google on Wednesday said it would withhold its most powerful artificial intelligence model from the public for now, releasing Gemini 4 Argon only to a vetted group of cybersecurity…
body: “Safely releasing frontier capabilities at this level requires a phased approach,” wrote Koray Kavukcuoglu, Google’s chief AI architect, in a blogpost announcing the model.
Google said it was voluntarily giving the US government early access to the model and would gather feedback from testers before making it widely available.
The cautious rollout mirrors the approach of rival Anthropic, which has kept its most advanced model, Claude Mythos Preview, restricted to a small number of trusted organizations.

Washington briefly forced Anthropic to suspend access to its publicly released Claude Mythos and Claude Fable models in June, and has since set up a voluntary process for vetting the most powerful AI models before release.

highlights.title: The eternal complement
highlights.summary: Advanced AI may matter most for the routine work behind breakthrough ideas. Explore why execution could shape the next economy and the pace of progress.
body: Authors’ note: This is the first essay in our series on the next economy, part of a new platform to host independent voices exploring an AGI future. It reflects our views, not those of OpenAI or our colleagues.

Our equations tell a mostly coherent account of the universe from its first moments. With our telescopes, we have looked to the reaches of the cosmos and glimpsed its early history. We know about the birth of stars and the formation of galaxies.
The explanations we seek span the universe, while our bodies have barely left home. Our minds venture way beyond the reach of our hands.

One possibility is that we needn’t go very far, that the deepest truths might be fathomed from a single planet. Armed with enlightened reasoning and efficient instruments, we reveal the universe without traversing it. In this story, our civilization advances through depth instead of width. It would help explain why we haven’t seen other intelligent life: we might live in a galaxy full of brilliant minds that never needed to expand and become noticeable to us.
points: Advanced AI may matter most for the routine work behind breakthrough ideas.

highlights.title: A 21st-Century Monster Masterpiece Will Return to Theaters in Glorious 4K
highlights.summary: One of the best films from acclaimed director Bong Joon Ho is returning to the big screen. The Host is getting a 4K remaster that's coming to theaters on Nov. 20, 2026.
body: The Host follows Gang-du (Song Kang-ho), a food stand worker who witnesses a massacre as a giant amphibian monster emerges from the Han River and attacks several bystanders, including his daughter. As the victims lie shell-shocked, the government announces that the monster is the host of an unidentified virus and quarantines the area. Then comes an unexpected twist. Gang-du inexplicably receives a call from his daughter, whom he thought was dead. The man resolves to find the monster and rescue his child while evading the government quarantine.

The Host was Bong's third feature-length film, following 2000’s Barking Dogs Never Bite and 2003’s Memories of Murder. This monster movie provided one of the highest-grossing South Korean pictures ever, making close to $100 million on an 11 billion won (roughly $11 million) budget while helping kickstart global viewership for Bong’s films. The movie received widespread critical praise for its mix of satire, humor, and monster-movie thrills. The Hos t is also known for its biting critique of American imperialism and for working as a 20th-century Godzilla equivalent.

highlights.title: With most information hidden, the game Stratego had stumped AI—until now
highlights.summary: Deep Blue took down Garry Kasparov at chess in 1997, AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol at Go in 2016, and poker bots have been beating professionals for years. But one classic game called Stratego held out.
body: Now, a team of researchers from Carnegie Mellon, MIT, New York University, and Stanford University has done it. Their AI, called Ataraxos, beat Pim Niemeijer, arguably the best Stratego player of all time, 15 games to one, with four draws. And it took just 16 GPUs and a few thousand dollars to train it.

In Stratego, each player gets 40 pieces representing military ranks, from a marshal down to a spy, plus bombs and a flag. You win by capturing the opponent's flag. Your opponent knows where your pieces are, but not what they are. Identities are revealed only when two pieces collide in battle—the weaker one is removed, and the identity of the winner is revealed. That makes Stratego an imperfect-information game, just like poker, which computers cracked years ago. “There's something super distinctive about Stratego, which is that it is a massive amount of hidden information that unfolds over a very long time scale,” said Eugene Vinitsky, a researcher at NYU and co-author of the study.

highlights.title: How Albertsons Companies is reimagining retail from the inside out
highlights.summary: Albertsons Cos. is using ChatGPT Enterprise and the OpenAI API to help teams work faster and make grocery shopping easier for millions of customers.
body: Albertsons Cos. is expanding its work with OpenAI to improve the retail experience for millions of customers.

Retail runs on small decisions made at enormous scale: which products to promote, how to help an associate, what a developer should build next—and, closer to home, what’s for dinner. Grocery shopping is one of the most ordinary ways we take care of ourselves and the people around us. At Albertsons Cos., these decisions play out across more than 2,200 stores, including Albertsons ®, Safeway ®, Vons ®, Jewel-Osco ®, Shaw’s ®, ACME ® and Tom Thumb ®, serving over 36 million customers each week.

OpenAI is working with Albertsons Cos. as the retailer continues to bring AI into everyday workflows, including ChatGPT Enterprise, as well as custom AI-powered experiences for its customers, data-driven recommendations and promotional insights built with the OpenAI API. The new Safeway experience in ChatGPT ⁠ (opens in a new window) brings that innovation to millions of shoppers, helping them move from a dinner idea to checkout all in ChatGPT.

highlights.summary: An opening text announcing “This film is influenced by real events” provides the first and last moment of inspiration in “The Influencer Project,” whether the joke is deliberate or not.
body: Copenhagen is to die for in Mike Nybroe’s decently crafted if over-familiar debut feature, in which Brit influencer Chiara King (playing herself) gets menaced by one very hostile, fictitious non-fan.

Yet as frightened as Chiara frequently is, and as concerned as the crew appear to be, somehow days keep going by without her ever thinking, “I gotta get the hell outta here.” When being hunted by a perp in a mask, what’s a person to do but dance at a nightclub where half the patrons are wearing glittery masks? Her follower count goes up whenever she appears scared. So even as danger rises, she visits “haunted houses” where something will inevitably get her running and screaming in dark corridors. Naturally, the climax takes place at a vast empty warehouse she and her remaining colleagues have been lured to. What could go wrong?

highlights.title: Terrible idea or major coup? Galliano’s Zara collection launches after Met controversy
highlights.summary: Collaboration regarded as ‘really big thing’ for retailer in some quarters despite backlash around designer’s antisemitic remarks in 2011. A month after it was announced that a planned exhibition dedicated to fashion designer John Galliano at New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art would not proceed…
body: Called Re{form}, it was, according to a press release, “authored by the couturier John Galliano. Built from our memory. Made for now.”

Its launch in shops comes after controversy over plans to honour the former Dior designer, who was found guilty of a hate crime in 2011 after a series of racist and antisemitic rants, with an exhibition of his work at the Met and a corresponding Met gala – a juggernaut of popular culture viewed by billions globally online. The exhibition was cancelled but had it gone ahead, it would have been only the third time such an honour had been bestowed on a living designer. The only others being Yves Saint Laurent in 1983 and Rei Kawakubo of Comme des Garçons in 2017.

The backlash to the plans were vehement and widespread, with Met patrons, New York politicians and prominent Jewish leaders objecting. Writing in the New York Times, his biographer Dana Thomas labelled it a “terrible idea”, saying that “choosing this moment to glorify the life’s work of someone who was convicted of making antisemitic remarks … is downright bizarre”, and noting that “his infamous antisemitic rants were not an aberration”.

highlights.title: OpenAI’s new agent is a shot at Meta — but can it compete with free?
highlights.summary: At OpenAI's annual DevDay conference, the company pulled out all the stops to compete with its rivals - primarily Meta, whose Muse AI agent platform has seen early runaway success.
body: OpenAI and Meta’s cutesy AI agents are about to fight to the death.

Muse’s main selling point is making AI agent access free and frictionless. The company offers a free dedicated virtual machine that houses both the agent and the user’s associated data. OpenAI’s Dots, by contrast, is restricted for now to users on its $20/month Pro plan and up. While anyone with a Meta account can get Muse, most of ChatGPT’s 1.2 billion users won’t be able to use Dots.

“Dots are starting out as a premium product — it uses a lot of compute,” Altman said Tuesday during a private press Q&A after his DevDay keynote, adding, “I think it will help us understand and help people understand how expansive and what AI can do. But you should of course expect us to do a mass-market thing for billions of people someday.”
The goal, Altman said, is to go beyond agents that simply book reservations, purchase meals, search calendars, and schedule appointments — classic use cases for consumer-facing tools like Muse.

highlights.title: Europe's CPC targets King, Supercell, Mojang and others over virtual currencies
highlights.summary: Europe's Consumer Protection Cooperation Network is taking "coordinated actions" against a string of top games companies as it looks to investigate compliance with 'Key Principles' on in-game virtual currencies announced last year.
body: The CPC is a network of national authorities responsible for the enforcement of EU consumer protection laws. It has asked Activision Blizzard, Crytek, InnoGames, King, Mojang, Plarium, PLR Worldwide Sales, Riot Games, Supercell and Ubisoft to bring their commercial practices in line relating to in-game virtual currencies.

Games being assessed include Hunt: Showdown 1896, Forge of Empires, Candy Crush Saga, Minecraft, Mech Arena, Gardenscapes, Valorant, Clash of Clans, For Honor, Diablo Immortal and Call of Duty Mobile.

The games were selected for assessment by the CPC Network "in the context of a wide-scale market compliance check due to broad reach, cross-device accessibility, and varied age ratings, all of which amplify the impact of the practices on consumers".
It's not clear what, if any, 'Key Principles' have not been adhered to prior to the CPC Network opening its investigations.

highlights.title: My wife obsessively consumes US news. She’s so stressed but can’t turn off. What should I do? | Leading questions
highlights.summary: Instead of asking her to step away from her distress, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith, could you suggest she channel it into action? My wife is obsessed with everything that’s happening in the US.
body: I’ve told her she needs to take at least one day off all social media, but she won’t do that even for an hour. It stresses her out more and more every day, but she just keeps going back to it – and it has been really affecting me, more lately than ever. On weekends I stay up late playing games (my way of winding down after a week of work) and she’ll go to bed early. And during those times sometimes I just sit and cry. Everything that’s happening is so stressful, and there’s nothing we can do about it. I just wish I could rip away her phone and let her breathe! I don’t know what to say or do. Is there anything that could help?

Eleanor says: It’s so easy to feel that if you’re a politically engaged person you have to stay tuned in and upset. The general collapse of everything is distressing. So it can seem like an obligation of responsible citizenship to be distressed.

highlights.title: Can VR glasses save VR?
highlights.summary: I'm pretty sure I won't be buying the $1,299 Meta VR Glasses. That's too rich for my blood in today's economy, and my feelings about Meta are… conflicted. But I want you to understand that Meta just changed the game. We've had glasses, but we've never had glasses like this.
body: Meta’s VR Glasses aren’t the glasses the industry promised. They might be better.

The Meta VR Glasses are not an opaque VR headset. They are not a pair of transparent AR glasses. They might be the best of both. After playing with the Meta VR Glasses, Valve’s Steam Frame, the Apple Vision Pro, and the Google / Xreal Aura back to back, I think they’re the first design that could convince regular people to give VR a chance.

It’s not because they look like glasses. It’s not just that they’re five times lighter than a typical headset at around 100 grams. It’s certainly not the $1,300 price tag, even if that’s much less than a $3,700 Vision Pro.
It’s about what you see and feel — and what you don’t see and feel — when you put Meta’s VR Glasses on your head.

highlights.summary: Lucasfilm veteran Kathleen Kennedy has admitted she feels "a bit of relief" after stepping down from her role as the boss of Star Wars, following a long and often tumultuous run.
body: Kennedy took Lucasfilm's helm in 2002 directly from Star Wars creator George Lucas, and oversaw the studio as it was sold to Disney, produced a new trilogy of mainline movies, and expanded its storytelling via an array of series on Disney+.

Some of these projects have been hugely successful, such as early seasons of The Mandalorian and the critically-acclaimed Andor. And while the Star Wars sequel movies ended in a firestorm of fan backlash and disappointment, they still raked in billions of dollars.

At the same time, numerous Star Wars projects have flopped hard — or simply failed to get off the ground. Solo was a commercial disaster and also messy behind the scenes, as acclaimed directors Phil Lord and Chris Miller (The Lego Movie, Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse) were ditched mid-way through filming. Gareth Edwards was reportedly replaced for Rogue One: A Star Wars Story reshoots, while Colin Trevorrow was replaced during the development of Episode 9.

highlights.title: Microsoft’s Office and Teams chief is leaving
highlights.summary: After nearly 18 years at LinkedIn and Microsoft, Ryan Roslansky is leaving the company. Roslansky, who until recently was the CEO of LinkedIn, was promoted to the head of Office last year and then took control of Microsoft Teams earlier this year.
body: Ryan Roslansky is leaving after nearly 18 years at LinkedIn and Microsoft.

“Ryan leaves the organization in a strong position,” says Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella in an internal memo. “Over the past year, Ryan’s team has done critical work bringing together the product, engineering, and design foundations that have made this next phase possible.”

Roslansky is leaving a week after Microsoft announced its new Copilot, which the company is positioning as “the OS for work.” He’s also leaving around a month after calling fully AI-generated documents “a doom loop” for workers. “If we’re not careful, we’ll end up with a very expensive way to avoid writing and reading in an ocean of sameness, genericness,” said Roslansky in his LinkedIn post.

Microsoft is now moving the teams behind Office and Microsoft Teams over to Charles Lamanna, as part of the Copilot, Agents, and Platform (CAP) organization. This is the second major reshuffling of the Office teams after Rajesh Jha, former head of Microsoft’s experiences and devices group, retired from Microsoft earlier this year.

body: The 56-year-old golfer voluntarily entered a treatment facility and has since returned home. Mickelson’s representatives did not say when he sought treatment or how long he stayed at a facility.

TMZ was the first to report the news. The six-time major winner, who has spoken in the past about gambling addiction, withdrew from the Masters in April and several LIV Golf events this year due to a “family health matter”.

In June, Mickelson denied allegations of nonconsensual and inappropriate physical conduct with a female employee at a San Diego golf club. A report by Golf Digest claimed Mickelson was challenged on an incident mid-round and left the property soon after. His lawyer confirmed he had resigned from the Farms Golf Club amid the allegations and said he was working on recovery.

“Some of the allegations circulating about Mr Mickelson are false, and others revisit mistakes he has already acknowledged, publicly or privately,” a spokesperson for Mickelson told People magazine in June, in response to an article on golf website Skratch about alleged misconduct.

highlights.summary: When life starts to feel boring, a touch of levity is just what the doctor ordered. Our contributors’ picks make even work and cleaning feel playful. A buckwheat pillow and 10lb blanket: what you loved most in September.
body: Welcome to Filter finds, a series where Filter contributors share the things they love most – and think you might, too.

The objects we choose to surround ourselves with should, above all, be useful – but life is short. Why not have a little fun while we’re at it? This month, we asked our contributors to share the practical things that spark not only joy, but whimsy – a sense of playfulness in our everyday lives. They certainly delivered!
From a toilet brush shaped like Excalibur to a concrete banana, these are the items our contributors use in pursuit of a whimsical life.

A couple in my town have installed some goose decoys in their front yard and dress them up thematically to delight passersby. And I am definitely delighted when I drive by and look to see what the “Nelsonville geese” are doing. They get dressed for holidays such as St Paddy’s Day, Cinco de Mayo (drinking Coronas), Fourth of July... and they have a Santa sleigh. They also do local things such as fishing in a baby pool to coincide with the local fish and game club’s fishing derby. They are hikers with trash strewn around their feet (a local peeve). During Covid, they social-distanced, 6ft apart.
